accessibility_rules: Describe labels, roles, announcements, and focus expectations.
component_contract.empty_state: Describe the empty state and what the user should understand from it.
component_contract.error_state: Describe the error state and available recovery path.

events_emitted.description: Primary event the component emits to its owner.
events_emitted.name: on_submit

keyboard_behavior: Describe keyboard shortcuts, focus movement, and submit/cancel behavior.
component_contract.loading_state: Describe the loading state and any placeholders or disabled actions.

props_needed.description: Primary props required to render the component.
props_needed.name: value

responsive_behavior: Describe breakpoint, pane-collapse, or overflow behavior.

state_needed.description: Primary state required to drive view behavior.
state_needed.name: view_state

expected_outputs.description: Validated component contract for Component Contract Template.
expected_outputs.name: component_contract

implementation_notes: Keep the contract specific enough that Dex can implement without inventing behavior.
State empty, loading, error, keyboard, and accessibility rules explicitly.
known_failure_modes: Component Contract Template omits state or event contracts, so the implementation guesses behavior.
Keyboard or accessibility rules are left implicit and regress later.
name: Component Contract Template
problem_solved: Turns Component Contract Template into a buildable contract instead of a vague component request.

required_inputs.description: State and signals required to render and act.
required_inputs.name: state_dependencies

summary: Machine-first template for buildable component contracts.
when_not_to_use: Do not use when Component Contract Template is too vague to state props, state, and emitted events.
Do not use when the true contract belongs at a larger feature boundary instead.
when_to_use: Use when Component Contract Template must be built from a concrete contract rather than a vague component request.
Use when props, state, events, keyboard rules, and tests need to be locked before coding.
